content: Taking this medication after your evening meal or at bedtime may help reduce stomach upset or nausea. However, you can choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. Your pill pack contains 26 active pills with hormones and 2 reminder pills without medication. Take one active pill daily for 26 consecutive days. After finishing the active pills, take one reminder pill daily for 2 days unless directed otherwise by your doctor. You should expect your period during the fourth week of the cycle. Once you finish the last reminder pill, start a new pack the next day, even if your period is still ongoing or has not started. If this is your first time using this medication and you are not switching from another form of hormonal birth control (e.g., patch or other pills), take the first tablet on the first day of your period. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on switching from other hormonal birth control methods to this product. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, abdominal cramps or bloating, breast tenderness, swelling of the ankles or feet (fluid retention), or weight changes. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may occur, especially during the first few months of use. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to estradiol, dienogest, other estrogens (e.g., mestranol), or progestins (e.g., norethindrone, desogestrel), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you have diabetes, this medication may affect your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. Inform your doctor if you have recently had or will be undergoing surgery, or if you will be confined to a bed or chair for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight). These conditions increase your risk of blood clots, especially if you are using hormonal birth control. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin (melasma), which can worsen with sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may develop vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. It may take longer to become pregnant after stopping birth control pills. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication may reduce breast milk production, and a small amount can pass into breast milk, potentially affecting a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., blood clotting factors, thyroid tests), potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular physical exams, including lab and medical tests (e.g. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, follow the instructions provided in the product package for your specific brand and the number of doses missed. You may need to use backup birth control (e.g., condoms, spermicide) to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: Do not use this medication if you smoke or use tobacco and are over 35 years old. This risk increases with age and the number of cigarettes smoked.
